1	// This file holds the shared core of single-decision review. The online
2	// Store.RecheckDecision and the store-free RecheckDecisionOffline acquire
3	// their material differently — one reads an organization's live history
4	// and version snapshots, the other a chain-validated export paired with its
5	// separately retained checkpoint — but once the recorded request and the
6	// version it actually used are in hand, both replay the exact same
7	// judgment. That judgment lives only here so the two entry points can never
8	// drift on version-zero handling, envelope rejection order, or how a
9	// historical policy set is evaluated.
10	package darksafe
11	
12	// replayStatus reports whether replayRecordedDecision produced a decision
13	// or why the declared version could not be replayed.
14	type replayStatus int
15	
16	const (
17		// replayDecided means a Decision was recomputed.
18		replayDecided replayStatus = iota
19		// replayVersionAbsent means content for the declared version exists
20		// nowhere in the reviewer's material.
21		replayVersionAbsent
22		// replayVersionAfterTarget means the version's content exists, but only
23		// in a policy change record positioned after the reviewed decision.
24		// Online material never yields this: live version snapshots carry no
25		// position relative to audit records.
26		replayVersionAfterTarget
27	)
28	
29	// versionPolicies is one resolver verdict: either the detached full policy
30	// set of the requested version, or a status explaining why it is unusable.
31	type versionPolicies struct {
32		policies []Policy
33		status   replayStatus
34	}
35	
36	// resolveVersionPolicies supplies the full content of a non-zero version
37	// named by a reviewed decision. Implementations are responsible for
38	// detaching the returned policies from any state or input material.
39	type resolveVersionPolicies func(version int) versionPolicies
40	
41	// replayRecordedDecision re-judges a recorded request against the version
42	// the record declares it actually used. Later publishes or rollbacks are
43	// never substituted for that version.
44	//
45	// A version-0 record first replays the envelope rejections in their fixed
46	// order (missing organizations and identifiers, empty action, organization
47	// mismatch, illegal scope, disabled subject); a request that passes is the
48	// "organization has no published version" denial.
49	//
50	// For a non-zero record the version is resolved before any request rule is
51	// applied: a missing, or only-later, version is an error the caller turns
52	// into ErrVersionNotFound and must never be masked by an envelope denial,
53	// even for a disabled subject. Once the version is in hand, the same
54	// envelope checks run before policy evaluation, so a rejection reports
55	// version 0 with no matched policies regardless of what the version
56	// contains. Evaluation itself is the historical policy set only: deny
57	// overrides allow, matched identifiers are sorted, resource restrictions
58	// narrow rather than replace scope matching, and subject roles never stand
59	// in for an organization policy.
60	func replayRecordedDecision(org string, req OrgRequest, version int, resolve resolveVersionPolicies) (Decision, replayStatus) {
61		if version == 0 {
62			// The original evaluation used no published version: replay the
63			// envelope rejections exactly, in their recorded order, then the
64			// not-yet-published denial.
65			if d, ok := checkRequest(org, req); !ok {
66				return d, replayDecided
67			}
68			return Decision{Allowed: false, Reason: "organization has no published version"}, replayDecided
69		}
70		// Resolve the version first. A request the envelope would reject must
71		// not turn a missing or later-only declared version into an ordinary
72		// denial.
73		resolved := resolve(version)
74		if resolved.status != replayDecided {
75			return Decision{}, resolved.status
76		}
77		// The version exists as claimed, but chain integrity does not imply the
78		// request was admissible: re-run the same envelope checks the online
79		// decision runs before any policy is consulted. A rejection here
80		// evaluates no policies, hence version 0 and no matches, even when the
81		// version holds a fully matching allow policy.
82		if d, ok := checkRequest(org, req); !ok {
83			return d, replayDecided
84		}
85		return evaluate(req, resolved.policies, version), replayDecided
86	}

1	// This file implements offline review of a single audited decision. It
2	// works solely from exported audit material: the complete record export,
3	// the separately retained checkpoint, and a target sequence. No Store is
4	// created or restored, so an organization can confirm why an access was
5	// allowed or denied long after the service instance that decided it has
6	// ended.
7	//
8	// The complete input must first validate as an audit chain. The policy
9	// version a decision actually used is recovered exclusively from policy
10	// change records preceding that decision within the same organization's
11	// export; later publishes or rollbacks, and a wider later export, cannot
12	// change the recomputed result.
13	package darksafe
14	
15	import "fmt"
16	
17	// OfflineDecisionReview compares the decision stored in an audited record
18	// with a decision recomputed purely from the exported material.
19	type OfflineDecisionReview struct {
20		// Seq is the reviewed decision record's sequence.
21		Seq int
22		// Original is the decision preserved in the audited record.
23		Original Decision
24		// Recomputed is the decision evaluated again offline from the saved
25		// request and the policy version it originally used.
26		Recomputed Decision
27		// Consistent reports whether both decisions agree on every field
28		// (allowance, reason, matched policies and version), treating a nil
29		// matched list and an empty matched list as the same.
30		Consistent bool
31	}
32	
33	// RecheckDecisionOffline re-evaluates one decision record offline. org is
34	// the organization name, records is its complete export starting at
35	// sequence 1 (a valid prefix is sufficient when paired with its own
36	// checkpoint), cp is the separately saved checkpoint, and seq identifies
37	// the decision record to review. The call is read-only: it neither mutates
38	// the supplied material nor appends audit records, and the returned
39	// decisions are detached from the input slices.
40	//
41	// The entire export is chain-validated before any result is produced;
42	// tampering anywhere, including in records after the target, fails the
43	// review. Distinguishable errors follow the other audit entry points:
44	// ErrMissingOrganization for an empty organization, ErrAuditNotFound for a
45	// non-positive or absent target sequence, and ErrAuditNotADecision when the
46	// target is a policy change record. When the saved decision names a
47	// policy version whose full content has no change record before the
48	// target, ErrVersionNotFound is returned; a newer version is never
49	// substituted, and a request the envelope would reject never masks the
50	// missing version.
51	//
52	// The fingerprint only proves the material matches its checkpoint; it
53	// cannot stand in for evaluating the request itself. So even when the
54	// declared version exists and carries an otherwise matching allow policy,
55	// the recomputation enforces the same request rules as the online
56	// decision: a disabled subject, an organization mismatch, a missing
57	// subject or resource organization or identifier, an empty action, and an
58	// illegal resource scope all deny, with the same reasons and precedence as
59	// Decide. Such a rejection uses no policies, so the recomputed decision
60	// reports version 0 with no matched policies; it is then compared field by
61	// field with the preserved original and may come back inconsistent.
62	func RecheckDecisionOffline(org string, records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint, seq int) (OfflineDecisionReview, error) {
63		if org == "" {
64			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, ErrMissingOrganization
65		}
66		// Validate the whole export first. A subject-filtered page, a fragment
67		// missing the beginning, or a checkpoint that does not pin the records
68		// all fail here, as does any corruption after the target.
69		if err := VerifyAudit(org, records, cp); err != nil {
70			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, err
71		}
72		if seq < 1 {
73			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: sequence %d", ErrAuditNotFound, seq)
74		}
75		if seq > len(records) {
76			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: export ends at %d, no sequence %d", ErrAuditNotFound, len(records), seq)
77		}
78		rec := &records[seq-1]
79		if rec.Kind != AuditDecision || rec.Decision == nil {
80			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: sequence %d is %s", ErrAuditNotADecision, seq, rec.Kind)
81		}
82	
83		original := cloneDecisionValue(rec.Decision.Decision)
84		req := rec.Decision.Request
85		// Detach the request list by non-nil rather than by length: a non-nil
86		// empty role list with spare capacity must not be shared back with the
87		// caller's material, even though evaluation never reads any element.
88		req.Subject.Roles = cloneStrings(req.Subject.Roles)
89		version := original.Version
90	
91		// The version's full content must travel in a same-organization policy
92		// change record positioned before the decision. The replay core resolves
93		// the version before replaying any request rule, so a request the
94		// envelope rejects cannot mask a missing or later-only version.
95		resolve := func(want int) versionPolicies {
96			if policies, found := policiesBefore(records, seq-1, want); found {
97				return versionPolicies{policies: policies}
98			}
99			if _, later := policiesBefore(records, len(records), want); later {
100				return versionPolicies{status: replayVersionAfterTarget}
101			}
102			return versionPolicies{status: replayVersionAbsent}
103		}
104		recomputed, status := replayRecordedDecision(org, req, version, resolve)
105		switch status {
106		case replayVersionAfterTarget:
107			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf(
108				"%w: decision at sequence %d used version %d, whose change record appears only after it",
109				ErrVersionNotFound, seq, version)
110		case replayVersionAbsent:
111			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf(
112				"%w: decision at sequence %d used version %d, which has no policy change record in the export",
113				ErrVersionNotFound, seq, version)
114		}
115	
116		return OfflineDecisionReview{
117			Seq:        seq,
118			Original:   original,
119			Recomputed: recomputed,
120			Consistent: decisionsEqual(original, recomputed),
121		}, nil
122	}
123	
124	// policiesBefore searches records[:limit] for the policy change record that
125	// published version and returns a detached copy of its full content. The
126	// gapless chain validation guarantees records are in sequence order.
127	func policiesBefore(records []AuditRecord, limit, version int) ([]Policy, bool) {
128		for i := 0; i < limit; i++ {
129			r := &records[i]
130			if r.Kind != AuditPolicyChange || r.Change == nil {
131				continue
132			}
133			if r.Change.Version == version {
134				return append([]Policy(nil), r.Change.Policies...), true
135			}
136		}
137		return nil, false
138	}
139	
140	// cloneDecisionValue returns a decision detached from the input's matched
141	// slice. The list is detached whenever it is non-nil, including a non-nil
142	// empty list that still has spare capacity, so an append by one receiver
143	// can never reach another copy.
144	func cloneDecisionValue(d Decision) Decision {
145		d.Matched = cloneStrings(d.Matched)
146		return d
147	}
148	
149	// decisionsEqual compares every decision field. A nil matched list and an
150	// empty matched list describe the same set of hits.
151	func decisionsEqual(a, b Decision) bool {
152		if a.Allowed != b.Allowed || a.Reason != b.Reason || a.Version != b.Version {
153			return false
154		}
155		if len(a.Matched) == 0 && len(b.Matched) == 0 {
156			return true
157		}
158		if len(a.Matched) != len(b.Matched) {
159			return false
160		}
161		for i := range a.Matched {
162			if a.Matched[i] != b.Matched[i] {
163				return false
164			}
165		}
166		return true
167	}

1	// This file implements the organization-scoped audit chain. Every successful
2	// policy publish or rollback, and every Decide called with a non-empty
3	// decision organization, leaves an immutable record in that organization.
4	//
5	// Records carry an organization-local sequence starting at 1 and a SHA-256
6	// fingerprint that chains each record to the previous one. The genesis
7	// fingerprint binds the organization name, so records from another
8	// organization can never validate as part of this chain even when the
9	// sequence numbers and identifiers coincide.
10	package darksafe
11	
12	import (
13		"crypto/sha256"
14		"encoding/binary"
15		"encoding/hex"
16		"encoding/json"
17		"errors"
18		"fmt"
19	)
20	
21	// Audit record categories.
22	const (
23		// AuditPolicyChange is a successful publish or rollback.
24		AuditPolicyChange = "policy_change"
25		// AuditDecision is one Decide evaluation.
26		AuditDecision = "decision"
27	)
28	
29	// Sentinel errors for the audit entry points. Callers distinguish them
30	// with errors.Is; every one leaves state unchanged.
31	var (
32		// ErrInvalidPage means a page size or range argument was invalid.
33		ErrInvalidPage = errors.New("darksafe: invalid audit page")
34		// ErrInvalidRange means the upper bound is beyond what exists, the
35		// range is inverted, or a supplied fingerprint does not match.
36		ErrInvalidRange = errors.New("darksafe: invalid audit range")
37		// ErrAuditNotFound means no record exists at the requested sequence.
38		ErrAuditNotFound = errors.New("darksafe: audit record not found")
39		// ErrAuditNotADecision means the record at the sequence is not a
40		// decision record and therefore cannot be rechecked.
41		ErrAuditNotADecision = errors.New("darksafe: audit record is not a decision")
42	)
43	
44	// PolicyChange captures a successful publish or rollback.
45	type PolicyChange struct {
46		// Version is the newly created policy version.
47		Version int
48		// Policies is the full policy set of the new version.
49		Policies []Policy
50		// SourceVersion is the version copied by a rollback, and 0 for an
51		// ordinary publish.
52		SourceVersion int
53		// RolledBack reports whether the change was produced by Rollback.
54		RolledBack bool
55	}
56	
57	// DecisionRecord captures one Decide call: the full request and the
58	// decision actually returned.
59	type DecisionRecord struct {
60		Request  OrgRequest
61		Decision Decision
62	}
63	
64	// AuditRecord is one immutable entry in an organization's audit chain.
65	type AuditRecord struct {
66		Org      string
67		Seq      int // organization-local, starting at 1 and gapless
68		Kind     string
69		Change   *PolicyChange   // present when Kind == AuditPolicyChange
70		Decision *DecisionRecord // present when Kind == AuditDecision
71	
72		// PrevFingerprint is the fingerprint of the preceding record, or the
73		// genesis fingerprint for the first record.
74		PrevFingerprint string
75		// Fingerprint binds this record's full content to its predecessor.
76		Fingerprint string
77	}
78	
79	// rawEnvelopePrefix opens every raw-byte canonical encoding. It never
80	// coincides with the start of a JSON envelope (always '{'), so
81	// fingerprints from the two encodings live in collision-free spaces.
82	const rawEnvelopePrefix = "darksafe-audit-raw-v1\x00"
83	
84	// fingerprintTag delimits one field or nested value within the canonical
85	// binary encoding. Distinct tags keep two payloads that merely share
86	// adjacent bytes apart (e.g. ["ab",""] vs ["a","b"]).
87	type fingerprintTag byte
88	
89	const (
90		tagEnvelope fingerprintTag = iota + 1
91		tagSeq
92		tagString
93		tagStringList
94		tagBool
95		tagPolicy
96		tagPolicyList
97		tagChange
98		tagSubject
99		tagResource
100		tagDecision
101		tagDecisionRecord
102	)
103	
104	// fingerprintEncoder builds the canonical byte representation of an
105	// envelope. Unlike encoding/json it writes string contents byte-for-byte
106	// with an explicit length prefix, so strings carrying invalid UTF-8 stay
107	// distinguishable: encoding/json renders both a raw 0xFF byte and a raw
108	// 0xFE byte as the U+FFFD replacement rune, collapsing genuinely
109	// different content onto identical fingerprints.
110	type fingerprintEncoder struct {
111		buf []byte
112	}
113	
114	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) tag(t fingerprintTag) {
115		e.buf = append(e.buf, byte(t))
116	}
117	
118	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) int64Tag(t fingerprintTag, v int64) {
119		e.tag(t)
120		var b [8]byte
121		binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(b[:], uint64(v))
122		e.buf = append(e.buf, b[:]...)
123	}
124	
125	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) boolTag(t fingerprintTag, v bool) {
126		e.tag(t)
127		if v {
128			e.buf = append(e.buf, 1)
129		} else {
130			e.buf = append(e.buf, 0)
131		}
132	}
133	
134	// rawString tags and writes a string from its exact memory bytes. No
135	// validation, replacement or normalization is ever performed: an invalid
136	// UTF-8 byte reaches the hash unchanged.
137	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) rawString(s string) {
138		e.tag(tagString)
139		var b [4]byte
140		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[:], uint32(len(s)))
141		e.buf = append(e.buf, b[:]...)
142		e.buf = append(e.buf, s...)
143	}
144	
145	// put appends one raw framing byte. It is the fingerprint sink's side of the
146	// shared list shape: the list presence marker goes into the canonical bytes
147	// verbatim.
148	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) put(b byte) {
149		e.buf = append(e.buf, b)
150	}
151	
152	// listCount writes a list element count as a big-endian uint32. The raw
153	// canonical encoding has no length ceiling beyond the hash input, so unlike
154	// the archive sink the count is written unconditionally; only the list shape
155	// (nil marker, presence marker, count then one item per element) is shared.
156	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) listCount(n int) {
157		var b [4]byte
158		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[:], uint32(n))
159		e.buf = append(e.buf, b[:]...)
160	}
161	
162	// stringList preserves nil-vs-empty explicitly: in the JSON envelope a
163	// nil slice is "null" and a non-nil empty slice is "[]", so the raw
164	// encoding must keep the two shapes apart as well. The list's own kind tag
165	// leads, then the shared list shape carries the presence marker, count and
166	// elements under it.
167	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) stringList(items []string) {
168		e.tag(tagStringList)
169		writeListShape(e, items, e.rawString)
170	}
171	
172	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) policy(p Policy) {
173		e.tag(tagPolicy)
174		// Field order, the Recursive boolean's position, and ResourceID being
175		// appended only when set all come from the single policy field table, so
176		// the fingerprint and the archive enumerate fields in exactly one place.
177		for i := range policyFields {
178			f := &policyFields[i]
179			switch f.kind {
180			case policyFieldString:
181				e.rawString(f.getString(p))
182			case policyFieldOptionalString:
183				// ResourceID participates only when set, pairing with its
184				// omitempty JSON tag, so the legacy fingerprint bytes are
185				// unchanged for resource-unrestricted policies.
186				if v := f.getString(p); v != "" {
187					e.rawString(v)
188				}
189			case policyFieldBool:
190				e.boolTag(tagBool, f.getBool(p))
191			}
192		}
193	}
194	
195	// policyList frames the full policy set with the shared list shape, led by
196	// the policy-list tag so a policy set can never collide with a string list
197	// whose concatenated bytes happen to match.
198	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) policyList(policies []Policy) {
199		e.tag(tagPolicyList)
200		writeListShape(e, policies, e.policy)
201	}
202	
203	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) change(c *PolicyChange) {
204		e.tag(tagChange)
205		// A nil pointer is encoded as tagChange alone; a present value's
206		// fields follow immediately.
207		if c == nil {
208			return
209		}
210		// Field order comes from the single policy-change field table, so the
211		// fingerprint, the UTF-8 decision, the archive and the detaching copy
212		// enumerate fields in exactly one place. No change field is skipped.
213		for i := range changeFields {
214			f := &changeFields[i]
215			switch f.kind {
216			case changeFieldInt:
217				e.int64Tag(tagSeq, int64(f.getInt(c)))
218			case changeFieldPolicyList:
219				e.policyList(f.getPolicies(c))
220			case changeFieldBool:
221				e.boolTag(tagBool, f.getBool(c))
222			}
223		}
224	}
225	
226	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) decisionRecord(d *DecisionRecord) {
227		e.tag(tagDecisionRecord)
228		if d == nil {
229			return
230		}
231		// Field order and the subject/resource/decision group markers all come
232		// from the single decision field table, so the fingerprint, the UTF-8
233		// decision and the archive enumerate fields in exactly one place. No
234		// request or decision field is skipped.
235		for i := range decisionFields {
236			f := &decisionFields[i]
237			if f.groupTag != 0 {
238				e.tag(f.groupTag)
239			}
240			switch f.kind {
241			case decisionFieldString:
242				e.rawString(f.getString(d))
243			case decisionFieldStringList:
244				e.stringList(f.getList(d))
245			case decisionFieldBool:
246				e.boolTag(tagBool, f.getBool(d))
247			case decisionFieldInt:
248				e.int64Tag(tagSeq, int64(f.getInt(d)))
249			}
250		}
251	}
252	
253	// encodeCanonical returns the raw bytes fingerprinted for a record whose
254	// strings include invalid UTF-8. Every string the record carries reaches
255	// the output byte-for-byte, at whatever nesting depth or list position it
256	// occupies. The prefix separates this encoding space from JSON
257	// fingerprints. The outer fields come from the single record field table,
258	// so this encoding enumerates exactly the envelope members the JSON
259	// encoding and the valid-UTF-8 scan see, in the same order.
260	func encodeCanonical(r *AuditRecord) []byte {
261		e := &fingerprintEncoder{buf: []byte(rawEnvelopePrefix)}
262		e.tag(tagEnvelope)
263		for i := range recordFields {
264			f := &recordFields[i]
265			if f.jsonKey == "" {
266				// The record's own fingerprint is never an input to itself.
267				continue
268			}
269			switch f.kind {
270			case recordFieldString:
271				e.rawString(f.getString(r))
272			case recordFieldInt:
273				e.int64Tag(tagSeq, int64(f.getInt(r)))
274			case recordFieldChange:
275				e.change(f.getChange(r))
276			case recordFieldDecision:
277				e.decisionRecord(f.getDecision(r))
278			}
279		}
280		return e.buf
281	}
282	
283	// genesisFingerprint derives the chain root from the organization name,
284	// keeping equal identifiers in different organizations independent.
285	func genesisFingerprint(org string) string {
286		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte("darksafe-audit-genesis\x00" + org))
287		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
288	}
289	
290	// encodeJSONEnvelope renders the fingerprint envelope of a record whose
291	// strings are all valid UTF-8 as the exact byte sequence the historical
292	// encoding/json envelope struct produced: the envelope members in the
293	// single record field table's order, every string, integer and payload
294	// encoded by encoding/json itself, and the two payload members dropped
295	// when absent exactly as their historical omitempty tags did. Walking the
296	// table keeps this object in lockstep with the raw canonical encoding, the
297	// valid-UTF-8 scan and the archive framing by construction.
298	func encodeJSONEnvelope(r *AuditRecord) []byte {
299		var buf []byte
300		buf = append(buf, '{')
301		first := true
302		for i := range recordFields {
303			f := &recordFields[i]
304			if f.jsonKey == "" {
305				// The record's own fingerprint is never an input to itself.
306				continue
307			}
308			var (
309				value []byte
310				err   error
311			)
312			switch f.kind {
313			case recordFieldString:
314				value, err = json.Marshal(f.getString(r))
315			case recordFieldInt:
316				value, err = json.Marshal(f.getInt(r))
317			case recordFieldChange:
318				c := f.getChange(r)
319				if c == nil {
320					continue
321				}
322				value, err = json.Marshal(c)
323			case recordFieldDecision:
324				d := f.getDecision(r)
325				if d == nil {
326					continue
327				}
328				value, err = json.Marshal(d)
329			}
330			if err != nil {
331				// All envelope values are plain, JSON-encodable values; a
332				// failure here indicates a programming error, not user input.
333				panic(fmt.Errorf("darksafe: audit envelope must encode: %w", err))
334			}
335			if !first {
336				buf = append(buf, ',')
337			}
338			first = false
339			buf = append(buf, '"')
340			buf = append(buf, f.jsonKey...)
341			buf = append(buf, '"', ':')
342			buf = append(buf, value...)
343		}
344		return append(buf, '}')
345	}
346	
347	// fingerprintFor returns the fingerprint for a record. Records made
348	// exclusively of valid UTF-8 keep the historical JSON fingerprint, so old
349	// exports and checkpoints remain valid; records containing invalid bytes
350	// use the length-prefixed raw encoding that protects their exact bytes.
351	// Both families cover exactly the envelope members of the single record
352	// field table — never the record's own fingerprint.
353	func fingerprintFor(r *AuditRecord) string {
354		if recordUsesRawBytes(r) {
355			sum := sha256.Sum256(encodeCanonical(r))
356			return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
357		}
358		sum := sha256.Sum256(encodeJSONEnvelope(r))
359		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
360	}
361	
362	// clonePolicies returns a detached copy of a policy set.
363	func clonePolicies(in []Policy) []Policy {
364		if in == nil {
365			return nil
366		}
367		return append([]Policy(nil), in...)
368	}
369	
370	// cloneChange returns a detached copy of a policy-change payload.
371	func cloneChange(c *PolicyChange) *PolicyChange {
372		if c == nil {
373			return nil
374		}
375		cp := *c
376		// Detach every list the single policy-change field table carries; the
377		// per-list nil-versus-empty handling stays exactly as clonePolicies
378		// defines it.
379		cloneChangeLists(&cp, c)
380		return &cp
381	}
382	
383	// cloneStrings returns a detached copy of a string slice while preserving
384	// its nil-versus-empty shape: a nil slice stays nil, and every non-nil
385	// slice, including a non-nil empty slice that still carries spare capacity,
386	// receives its own backing array. Copying only when len > 0 is not enough:
387	// a caller may submit make([]string, 0, 4), and aliasing that array into a
388	// stored record would let an append to one handed-out copy overwrite the
389	// first element of every other copy that shares it.
390	func cloneStrings(in []string) []string {
391		if in == nil {
392			return nil
393		}
394		return append([]string{}, in...)
395	}
396	
397	// cloneDecision returns a detached copy of a decision payload.
398	func cloneDecision(d *DecisionRecord) *DecisionRecord {
399		if d == nil {
400			return nil
401		}
402		cp := *d
403		// Detach every list the single decision field table carries, on non-nil
404		// rather than on len > 0 so empty-but-capacious lists are independent
405		// copies too; nil lists stay nil.
406		cloneDecisionLists(&cp, d)
407		return &cp
408	}
409	
410	// cloneRecord returns a fully detached copy of a record.
411	func cloneRecord(r *AuditRecord) *AuditRecord {
412		cp := *r
413		cp.Change = cloneChange(r.Change)
414		cp.Decision = cloneDecision(r.Decision)
415		return &cp
416	}
417	
418	// appendAuditLocked validates, fingerprints and stores one record. It runs
419	// under the store mutex and is the single place records are created.
420	func (st *orgState) appendAuditLocked(org, kind string, change *PolicyChange, decision *DecisionRecord) *AuditRecord {
421		seq := len(st.audit) + 1
422		prev := genesisFingerprint(org)
423		if len(st.audit) > 0 {
424			prev = st.audit[len(st.audit)-1].Fingerprint
425		}
426		// Store detached copies; later caller mutation must not reach the chain.
427		rec := &AuditRecord{
428			Org:             org,
429			Seq:             seq,
430			Kind:            kind,
431			Change:          cloneChange(change),
432			Decision:        cloneDecision(decision),
433			PrevFingerprint: prev,
434		}
435		rec.Fingerprint = fingerprintFor(rec)
436		st.audit = append(st.audit, rec)
437		return cloneRecord(rec)
438	}
439	
440	// auditHeadLocked returns the highest sequence in the chain and the
441	// fingerprint that covers it: (0, genesis) for an organization with no
442	// records.
443	func (st *orgState) auditHeadLocked(org string) (int, string) {
444		if len(st.audit) == 0 {
445			return 0, genesisFingerprint(org)
446		}
447		last := st.audit[len(st.audit)-1]
448		return last.Seq, last.Fingerprint
449	}
450	
451	// Checkpoint pins an audit query to an exact point in a chain.
452	type Checkpoint struct {
453		Org         string
454		EndSeq      int
455		Fingerprint string
456	}
457	
458	// AuditPage is one stable slice of an organization's audit chain.
459	type AuditPage struct {
460		Org     string
461		Records []AuditRecord
462		// BeginSeq/EndSeq delimit the whole pinned range, not just this page.
463		BeginSeq int
464		EndSeq   int
465		// Next is the first sequence of the following page, 0 when exhausted.
466		Next int
467		// Checkpoint is the pinned upper bound shared by every page.
468		Checkpoint Checkpoint
469	}
470	
471	// recordMatches reports whether a record survives the query filters. Every
472	// set filter is a conjunction: kind, subject and resource conditions must
473	// all hold. Empty filter values mean "not set".
474	func recordMatches(r *AuditRecord, kind, subjectID, resourceID string) bool {
475		if kind != "" && r.Kind != kind {
476			return false
477		}
478		if subjectID != "" {
479			// A subject filter selects decision records of that subject only.
480			if r.Kind != AuditDecision || r.Decision == nil ||
481				r.Decision.Request.Subject.ID != subjectID {
482				return false
483			}
484		}
485		if resourceID != "" {
486			// A resource filter selects decision records whose request named
487			// exactly this resource. Policy-change records never match, even when
488			// a published policy carries the identical ResourceID: the condition
489			// reads the requested resource, not policy content. The comparison is
490			// Go string equality over the stored raw bytes, so case, surrounding
491			// and internal spaces, control bytes and invalid UTF-8 are all
492			// significant, and no path or wildcard is interpreted.
493			if r.Kind != AuditDecision || r.Decision == nil ||
494				r.Decision.Request.Resource.ID != resourceID {
495				return false
496			}
497		}
498		return true
499	}
500	
501	// optionalResourceCondition extracts the optional resource condition passed
502	// as the trailing variadic argument. An absent argument or an empty string
503	// means "no resource filter"; supplying more than one condition is a caller
504	// error rather than a silently picked value.
505	func optionalResourceCondition(conds []string) (string, error) {
506		switch len(conds) {
507		case 0:
508			return "", nil
509		case 1:
510			return conds[0], nil
511		default:
512			return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: at most one resource condition may be set, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, len(conds))
513		}
514	}
515	
516	// AuditQuery pins the first page of an audit query. startSeq is the first
517	// sequence considered (1 from the beginning); endSeq <= 0 means "everything
518	// currently stored". The returned checkpoint must be passed to AuditPage
519	// for the following pages, so records appended after the first query never
520	// mix into later pages.
521	//
522	// kind and subjectID are the existing optional filters (empty means unset):
523	// kind selects a record category and subjectID selects one subject's
524	// decision records. The optional trailing resourceID adds a resource
525	// condition, empty or absent meaning unset: only decision records whose
526	// requested resource ID equals it byte-for-byte survive — case sensitive,
527	// spaces and control bytes significant, no path or wildcard interpretation,
528	// invalid UTF-8 kept as-is — and policy-change records never survive it,
529	// even when a published policy names the same resource ID. Every set
530	// condition applies together. A resource filter changes only which records
531	// are returned: paging, checkpoints and detached copies behave exactly as
532	// without it, and omitting it preserves the historical call and its results.
533	func (s *Store) AuditQuery(org string, startSeq, pageSize int, kind, subjectID string, resourceID ...string) (*AuditPage, error) {
534		resource, err := optionalResourceCondition(resourceID)
535		if err != nil {
536			return nil, err
537		}
538		if org == "" {
539			return nil, ErrMissingOrganization
540		}
541		if kind != "" && kind != AuditPolicyChange && kind != AuditDecision {
542			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unknown category %q", ErrInvalidPage, kind)
543		}
544		if pageSize <= 0 {
545			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: page size must be positive, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, pageSize)
546		}
547		if startSeq < 1 {
548			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: start sequence must be >= 1, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, startSeq)
549		}
550		s.mu.Lock()
551		defer s.mu.Unlock()
552		st := s.orgLocked(org)
553		end, fingerprint := st.auditHeadLocked(org)
554		cp := Checkpoint{Org: org, EndSeq: end, Fingerprint: fingerprint}
555		if end == 0 {
556			// An organization with no records always yields the empty genesis
557			// page, regardless of where the caller asked to begin.
558			return &AuditPage{Org: org, BeginSeq: 1, EndSeq: 0, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
559		}
560		if startSeq > end {
561			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: start sequence %d is beyond end sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, startSeq, end)
562		}
563		return s.auditPageLocked(org, startSeq, end, fingerprint, pageSize, kind, subjectID, resource), nil
564	}
565	
566	// AuditPage returns one page of a previously pinned query. nextSeq is the
567	// cursor from the previous page; when it is 0 the range is exhausted. The
568	// checkpoint is re-verified against the chain on every call.
569	//
570	// The filters are the same as AuditQuery's and must agree with the pinned
571	// query: pass the same kind, subjectID and optional resourceID on every
572	// page. The resource condition is an exact raw-byte match over requested
573	// resource IDs and excludes policy-change records, exactly as on the first
574	// page; omitting it keeps the historical call and result shape.
575	func (s *Store) AuditPage(cp Checkpoint, nextSeq, pageSize int, kind, subjectID string, resourceID ...string) (*AuditPage, error) {
576		resource, err := optionalResourceCondition(resourceID)
577		if err != nil {
578			return nil, err
579		}
580		if cp.Org == "" {
581			return nil, ErrMissingOrganization
582		}
583		if kind != "" && kind != AuditPolicyChange && kind != AuditDecision {
584			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unknown category %q", ErrInvalidPage, kind)
585		}
586		if pageSize <= 0 {
587			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: page size must be positive, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, pageSize)
588		}
589		if nextSeq < 0 {
590			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: next sequence must be >= 0, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, nextSeq)
591		}
592		s.mu.Lock()
593		defer s.mu.Unlock()
594		st, ok := s.orgs[cp.Org]
595		if !ok {
596			// No organization state: the only valid checkpoint is an empty one.
597			g := genesisFingerprint(cp.Org)
598			if cp.EndSeq == 0 && cp.Fingerprint == g && nextSeq == 0 {
599				return &AuditPage{Org: cp.Org, BeginSeq: 0, EndSeq: 0, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
600			}
601			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint organization has no records", ErrInvalidRange)
602		}
603		head := len(st.audit)
604		if cp.EndSeq < 0 || cp.EndSeq > head {
605			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence %d beyond %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq, head)
606		}
607		wantFP := genesisFingerprint(cp.Org)
608		if cp.EndSeq > 0 {
609			if cp.EndSeq > len(st.audit) {
610				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence %d beyond %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq, head)
611			}
612			wantFP = st.audit[cp.EndSeq-1].Fingerprint
613		}
614		if cp.Fingerprint != wantFP {
615			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint fingerprint does not match the chain at sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq)
616		}
617		if nextSeq == 0 {
618			return &AuditPage{Org: cp.Org, BeginSeq: 1, EndSeq: cp.EndSeq, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
619		}
620		if nextSeq > cp.EndSeq+1 {
621			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: next sequence %d beyond pinned range ending at %d", ErrInvalidRange, nextSeq, cp.EndSeq)
622		}
623		if nextSeq == cp.EndSeq+1 {
624			return &AuditPage{Org: cp.Org, BeginSeq: nextSeq, EndSeq: cp.EndSeq, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
625		}
626		return s.auditPageLocked(cp.Org, nextSeq, cp.EndSeq, wantFP, pageSize, kind, subjectID, resource), nil
627	}
628	
629	// auditPageLocked scans forward collecting up to pageSize matching records
630	// and computes the next-page cursor. It does not stop at pageSize raw
631	// records: filtering happens within the pinned [start,end] window, so
632	// non-matching records between matches — including policy changes excluded
633	// by a resource condition — never consume page slots.
634	func (s *Store) auditPageLocked(org string, startSeq, endSeq int, endFP string, pageSize int, kind, subjectID, resourceID string) *AuditPage {
635		st := s.orgs[org]
636		// pageSize only bounds how many records this page returns; it must not
637		// drive allocation. A caller may pass any positive value, including the
638		// largest int, for a range holding a handful of records, so preallocate
639		// no more than the window can actually contain.
640		window := endSeq - startSeq + 1
641		capHint := pageSize
642		if window < capHint {
643			capHint = window
644		}
645		out := make([]AuditRecord, 0, capHint)
646		i := startSeq
647		for ; i <= endSeq && len(out) < pageSize; i++ {
648			r := st.audit[i-1]
649			if recordMatches(r, kind, subjectID, resourceID) {
650				out = append(out, *cloneRecord(r))
651			}
652		}
653		next := 0
654		if i <= endSeq {
655			next = i
656		}
657		return &AuditPage{
658			Org:        org,
659			Records:    out,
660			BeginSeq:   startSeq,
661			EndSeq:     endSeq,
662			Next:       next,
663			Checkpoint: Checkpoint{Org: org, EndSeq: endSeq, Fingerprint: endFP},
664		}
665	}
666	
667	// AuditExport returns detached copies of the complete records through
668	// endSeq, suitable for offline verification. endSeq <= 0 means everything
669	// currently stored. An organization with no records yields an empty slice
670	// together with its sequence-0 checkpoint.
671	func (s *Store) AuditExport(org string, endSeq int) (records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint, err error) {
672		if org == "" {
673			return nil, Checkpoint{}, ErrMissingOrganization
674		}
675		s.mu.Lock()
676		defer s.mu.Unlock()
677		st := s.orgLocked(org)
678		head := len(st.audit)
679		if endSeq <= 0 {
680			endSeq = head
681		}
682		if endSeq > head {
683			return nil, Checkpoint{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence %d beyond %d", ErrInvalidRange, endSeq, head)
684		}
685		if endSeq < 0 {
686			return nil, Checkpoint{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence must be >= 0, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, endSeq)
687		}
688		// The checkpoint fingerprints the final exported record, not the
689		// possibly later current head.
690		fingerprint := genesisFingerprint(org)
691		if endSeq > 0 {
692			fingerprint = st.audit[endSeq-1].Fingerprint
693		}
694		out := make([]AuditRecord, 0, endSeq)
695		for i := 0; i < endSeq; i++ {
696			out = append(out, *cloneRecord(st.audit[i]))
697		}
698		return out, Checkpoint{Org: org, EndSeq: endSeq, Fingerprint: fingerprint}, nil
699	}
700	
701	// VerifyAudit validates an exported record set entirely without a Store.
702	// The caller separately retains the organization, end sequence and
703	// fingerprint they expect. It rejects any modified field, missing middle or
704	// tail record, swapped order, and record spliced in from another
705	// organization. Empty or nil records validate exactly when the checkpoint
706	// is the organization's genesis (end sequence 0).
707	func VerifyAudit(org string, records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint) error {
708		if org == "" {
709			return ErrMissingOrganization
710		}
711		if cp.Org != "" && cp.Org != org {
712			return fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint organization %q does not match %q", ErrInvalidRange, cp.Org, org)
713		}
714		genesis := genesisFingerprint(org)
715		if len(records) == 0 {
716			if cp.EndSeq != 0 || cp.Fingerprint != genesis {
717				return fmt.Errorf("%w: empty records but checkpoint claims end sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq)
718			}
719			return nil
720		}
721		if cp.EndSeq != len(records) {
722			return fmt.Errorf("%w: have %d records, checkpoint ends at %d", ErrInvalidRange, len(records), cp.EndSeq)
723		}
724		prev := genesis
725		for i, r := range records {
726			wantSeq := i + 1
727			if r.Org != org {
728				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d belongs to organization %q", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq, r.Org)
729			}
730			if r.Seq != wantSeq {
731				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d has sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq, r.Seq)
732			}
733			if r.PrevFingerprint != prev {
734				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d breaks the chain", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
735			}
736			wantFP := fingerprintFor(&r)
737			if r.Fingerprint != wantFP {
738				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d fingerprint mismatch", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
739			}
740			if r.Kind == AuditPolicyChange {
741				if r.Change == nil || r.Decision != nil {
742					return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d payload does not match its category", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
743				}
744			} else if r.Kind == AuditDecision {
745				if r.Decision == nil || r.Change != nil {
746					return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d payload does not match its category", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
747				}
748			} else {
749				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d has unknown category %q", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq, r.Kind)
750			}
751			prev = r.Fingerprint
752		}
753		last := records[len(records)-1]
754		if last.Fingerprint != cp.Fingerprint {
755			return fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint fingerprint does not match the final record", ErrInvalidRange)
756		}
757		return nil
758	}
759	
760	// RecheckDecision re-evaluates the request stored in an organization's
761	// decision record against the policy version that decision actually used.
762	// Later publishes or rollbacks cannot alter the result. Non-decision
763	// records and missing sequences return distinguishable errors.
764	//
765	// The record and the version snapshot come exclusively from this
766	// organization's own live history; the version-zero and historical-policy
767	// judgment itself is shared with RecheckDecisionOffline in
768	// replayRecordedDecision.
769	func (s *Store) RecheckDecision(org string, seq int) (Decision, error) {
770		if org == "" {
771			return Decision{}, ErrMissingOrganization
772		}
773		if seq < 1 {
774			return Decision{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: sequence %d", ErrAuditNotFound, seq)
775		}
776		s.mu.Lock()
777		defer s.mu.Unlock()
778		st, ok := s.orgs[org]
779		if !ok || seq > len(st.audit) {
780			return Decision{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: organization %q has no audit sequence %d", ErrAuditNotFound, org, seq)
781		}
782		rec := st.audit[seq-1]
783		if rec.Kind != AuditDecision || rec.Decision == nil {
784			return Decision{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: sequence %d is %s", ErrAuditNotADecision, seq, rec.Kind)
785		}
786		req := rec.Decision.Request
787		version := rec.Decision.Decision.Version
788		resolve := func(version int) versionPolicies {
789			src, ok := st.versions[version]
790			if !ok {
791				// A decision's version is immutable and never deleted; its
792				// absence indicates store tampering rather than normal
793				// operation.
794				return versionPolicies{status: replayVersionAbsent}
795			}
796			// Live snapshots are immutable; detach anyway so the returned
797			// decision can never share storage with the store.
798			return versionPolicies{policies: append([]Policy(nil), src...)}
799		}
800		d, status := replayRecordedDecision(org, req, version, resolve)
801		if status == replayVersionAbsent {
802			return Decision{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: decision used version %d, which no longer exists", ErrVersionNotFound, version)
803		}
804		return d, nil
805	}

1	// The review subcommand re-evaluates one decision preserved in an audit
2	// archive after the service instance that decided it has ended. It never
3	// talks to a running service and never creates or restores a Store: the
4	// decision is recomputed purely from the saved record's request, the
5	// historical policy version carried in records before it, and a checkpoint
6	// the caller retained separately from the archive.
7	package main
8	
9	import (
10		"errors"
11		"fmt"
12		"io"
13		"os"
14		"strconv"
15		"strings"
16	
17		"github.com/asdhoaiqqq/darksafe-access/darksafe"
18	)
19	
20	// Exit codes for the review command:
21	//
22	//   - 0: a full review was produced and the complete report was written
23	//     without error, including a legitimate archive whose original and
24	//     recomputed decisions disagree.
25	//   - 2: the invocation itself is wrong (missing/invalid arguments, the
26	//     archive file cannot be read).
27	//   - 1: the material or target cannot support a review (an invalid or
28	//     chain-broken archive, a missing or non-decision target, a historical
29	//     policy version that cannot be obtained), or the review report could
30	//     not be written out in full.
31	const (
32		reviewExitOK     = 0
33		reviewExitFailed = 1
34		reviewExitUsage  = 2
35	)
36	
37	// reviewInputs holds everything the review command needs from the caller.
38	type reviewInputs struct {
39		archivePath string
40		org         string
41		seq         int
42		endSeq      int
43		fingerprint string
44		// json selects machine-readable JSON output instead of the default text
45		// report. The review itself is identical either way: the same archive
46		// validation and the same historical recheck, never a re-submitted
47		// request.
48		json bool
49	}
50	
51	func reviewHelp(w io.Writer) {
52		fmt.Fprint(w, `usage: darksafe review --archive FILE --org ORG --seq N \
53	                      --end-seq N --fingerprint HEX
54	
55	Review one access decision saved in an audit archive, long after the
56	service instance that made the decision has ended. No running service is
57	contacted and no policy store is created or restored; the decision is
58	recomputed offline from the archived material alone. The archived decision
59	is never re-submitted as a new access request.
60	
61	Required inputs:
62	  --archive FILE       path to the audit archive written by
63	                       EncodeAuditArchive (the complete export, not a
64	                       subject-filtered page or a fragment)
65	  --org ORG            organization name the archive belongs to; it must
66	                       match the organization bound into the records
67	  --seq N              positive sequence number of the decision record to
68	                       review (organization-local, starting at 1)
69	  --end-seq N          end sequence of the checkpoint retained separately
70	                       from the archive (0 for an organization with no
71	                       records); must not be negative
72	  --fingerprint HEX    checkpoint fingerprint retained separately from the
73	                       archive (64 hexadecimal SHA-256 characters)
74	  --json               emit the review as one complete JSON object on
75	                       stdout instead of the text report. The object gives
76	                       "target_sequence", "original" and "recomputed"
77	                       decisions (each with "allowed", "reason",
78	                       "matched_policies" in original order, and
79	                       "policy_version"), and "consistent". A valid UTF-8
80	                       string is a JSON string; a string that is not valid
81	                       UTF-8 is the object {"base64": "<standard base64 of
82	                       the exact bytes>"}, so a lone 0xFF, a lone 0xFE and a
83	                       real U+FFFD never collapse together and every string's
84	                       original bytes can be recovered. A nil and an empty
85	                       matched list both render as []. A failure before the
86	                       report is written leaves stdout empty and the reason on
87	                       stderr only; if stdout refuses the report or accepts
88	                       only part of it, any accepted prefix stays in place,
89	                       the command exits 1 and the output failure is reported
90	                       on stderr, never retried in another format.
91	
92	The checkpoint carried inside the archive is informational only: validation
93	always uses --end-seq/--fingerprint supplied here. Even when --seq points at
94	an early record, every archived record is checked; a corrupted or missing
95	later record, or any mismatch with the retained checkpoint, fails the whole
96	review with no partial output.
97	
98	The request is replayed strictly against the policy version the recorded
99	decision actually used; later publishes or rollbacks present in the archive
100	are never substituted. A chain that is valid but whose original and
101	recomputed decisions disagree is still printed in full and exits 0; the
102	disagreement is shown explicitly rather than reported as file damage.
103	
104	Strings may contain spaces, control characters or non-UTF-8 bytes; the text
105	report uses Go-style quoting, while --json uses the JSON string /
106	{"base64": ...} rule described above, and both keep different raw bytes
107	distinguishable. This command only reads the named archive: it neither
108	rewrites it nor appends audit records.
109	
110	Exit codes: 0 complete report written without error (decisions may
111	disagree), 1 archive or target invalid / historical version unavailable /
112	review report could not be written out in full, 2 bad arguments or
113	unreadable file. --json changes none of these.
114	
115	Example:
116	  (materials produced by examples/offline_review; seq 1 is the
117	  policy publish record, seq 2 is the read decision being reviewed)
118	  darksafe review --archive acme-factory.audit \
119	      --org 'acme factory' --seq 2 --end-seq 2 \
120	      --fingerprint 04b274dbb4cf039bbb4b78f5ee5aae03278d2c34833fe87fecb13ade51ef5299
121	
122	  add --json to get the same review as one JSON object:
123	  darksafe review --json --archive acme-factory.audit \
124	      --org 'acme factory' --seq 2 --end-seq 2 \
125	      --fingerprint 04b274dbb4cf039bbb4b78f5ee5aae03278d2c34833fe87fecb13ade51ef5299
126	`)
127	}
128	
129	// parseReviewArgs parses review arguments. flags is an injectable args slice
130	// so tests can drive the command directly. The first element of args is the
131	// subcommand name ("review"). --help/-h/-help set wantHelp.
132	func parseReviewArgs(args []string) (in reviewInputs, wantHelp bool, err error) {
133		haveSeq, haveEndSeq := false, false
134		for i := 1; i < len(args); i++ {
135			arg := args[i]
136			value := ""
137			hasValue := false
138			switch {
139			case arg == "--help" || arg == "-h" || arg == "-help":
140				return reviewInputs{}, true, nil
141			case len(arg) > 2 && arg[:2] == "--":
142				// Accept both --flag value and --flag=value.
143				if eq := strings.IndexByte(arg, '='); eq >= 0 {
144					value = arg[eq+1:]
145					hasValue = true
146					arg = arg[:eq]
147				}
148			default:
149				return reviewInputs{}, false, fmt.Errorf("unexpected argument %q", arg)
150			}
151	
152			take := func() (string, error) {
153				if hasValue {
154					return value, nil
155				}
156				if i+1 >= len(args) {
157					return "", fmt.Errorf("flag %s requires a value", arg)
158				}
159				i++
160				return args[i], nil
161			}
162	
163			switch arg {
164			case "--archive":
165				v, err := take()
166				if err != nil {
167					return reviewInputs{}, false, err
168				}
169				in.archivePath = v
170			case "--org":
171				v, err := take()
172				if err != nil {
173					return reviewInputs{}, false, err
174				}
175				in.org = v
176			case "--seq":
177				v, err := take()
178				if err != nil {
179					return reviewInputs{}, false, err
180				}
181				n, perr := strconv.Atoi(v)
182				if perr != nil {
183					return reviewInputs{}, false, fmt.Errorf("--seq must be an integer, got %q", v)
184				}
185				in.seq = n
186				haveSeq = true
187			case "--end-seq":
188				v, err := take()
189				if err != nil {
190					return reviewInputs{}, false, err
191				}
192				n, perr := strconv.Atoi(v)
193				if perr != nil {
194					return reviewInputs{}, false, fmt.Errorf("--end-seq must be an integer, got %q", v)
195				}
196				in.endSeq = n
197				haveEndSeq = true
198			case "--fingerprint":
199				v, err := take()
200				if err != nil {
201					return reviewInputs{}, false, err
202				}
203				in.fingerprint = v
204			case "--json":
205				// Bare --json enables JSON output; --json=value accepts the
206				// usual boolean spellings. No value is ever consumed from the
207				// following token, so "--json --seq 2" keeps working.
208				switch {
209				case !hasValue:
210					in.json = true
211				default:
212					b, perr := strconv.ParseBool(value)
213					if perr != nil {
214						return reviewInputs{}, false, fmt.Errorf("--json must be a boolean, got %q", value)
215					}
216					in.json = b
217				}
218			default:
219				return reviewInputs{}, false, fmt.Errorf("unknown review flag %q", arg)
220			}
221		}
222	
223		if in.archivePath == "" {
224			return reviewInputs{}, false, errors.New("--archive is required")
225		}
226		if in.org == "" {
227			return reviewInputs{}, false, errors.New("--org is required")
228		}
229		if !haveSeq {
230			return reviewInputs{}, false, errors.New("--seq is required")
231		}
232		if in.seq <= 0 {
233			return reviewInputs{}, false, fmt.Errorf("--seq must be a positive integer, got %d", in.seq)
234		}
235		if !haveEndSeq {
236			return reviewInputs{}, false, errors.New("--end-seq is required")
237		}
238		if in.endSeq < 0 {
239			return reviewInputs{}, false, fmt.Errorf("--end-seq must not be negative, got %d", in.endSeq)
240		}
241		if in.fingerprint == "" {
242			return reviewInputs{}, false, errors.New("--fingerprint is required")
243		}
244		return in, false, nil
245	}
246	
247	// runReview executes one offline review and returns the process exit code.
248	// stdout/stderr are injectable so the command stays testable; args is the
249	// full argument vector including the leading "review".
250	func runReview(args []string, stdout, stderr io.Writer) int {
251		in, wantHelp, err := parseReviewArgs(args)
252		if wantHelp {
253			reviewHelp(stdout)
254			return reviewExitOK
255		}
256		if err != nil {
257			fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "review: %s\n", err)
258			return reviewExitUsage
259		}
260	
261		archive, err := os.ReadFile(in.archivePath)
262		if err != nil {
263			fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "review: cannot read archive %q: %v\n", in.archivePath, err)
264			return reviewExitUsage
265		}
266	
267		cp := darksafe.Checkpoint{Org: in.org, EndSeq: in.endSeq, Fingerprint: in.fingerprint}
268		records, err := darksafe.DecodeAuditArchive(archive, in.org, cp)
269		if err != nil {
270			fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "review: archive validation failed: %v\n", err)
271			return reviewExitFailed
272		}
273		review, err := darksafe.RecheckDecisionOffline(in.org, records, cp, in.seq)
274		if err != nil {
275			fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "review: %v\n", err)
276			return reviewExitFailed
277		}
278	
279		// Render both formats fully before touching stdout: a render failure must
280		// not leave partial output, and every earlier failure path already
281		// returned with stdout untouched.
282		var payload []byte
283		if in.json {
284			payload, err = renderReviewJSON(review)
285			if err != nil {
286				fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "review: cannot encode result as JSON: %v\n", err)
287				return reviewExitFailed
288			}
289		} else {
290			var buf strings.Builder
291			printReview(&buf, review)
292			payload = []byte(buf.String())
293		}
294	
295		// Success requires the WHOLE report to actually land. A receiver may
296		// accept some bytes and then refuse the rest, or report a short write
297		// with no error; neither may be mistaken for a completed review merely
298		// because the archive validated and the decision recomputed. Whatever
299		// prefix the receiver already accepted stays there (it cannot be
300		// unwritten), but nothing more is appended afterwards.
301		n, werr := stdout.Write(payload)
302		if werr != nil {
303			fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "review: failed to write review report: %v\n", werr)
304			return reviewExitFailed
305		}
306		if n < len(payload) {
307			fmt.Fprintf(stderr,
308				"review: review report output incomplete: wrote %d of %d bytes\n",
309				n, len(payload))
310			return reviewExitFailed
311		}
312		return reviewExitOK
313	}
314	
315	// printReview renders the target sequence, both full decisions and the
316	// consistency verdict. Every potentially non-UTF-8 string is emitted with
317	// %q (Go quoting): a lone 0xFF renders as "\xff", 0xFE as "\xfe" and a real
318	// U+FFFD as "�", so distinct raw bytes never collapse onto one glyph.
319	func printReview(w io.Writer, r darksafe.OfflineDecisionReview) {
320		fmt.Fprintf(w, "target sequence: %d\n", r.Seq)
321		fmt.Fprintln(w, "original decision:")
322		printDecision(w, r.Original)
323		fmt.Fprintln(w, "recomputed decision:")
324		printDecision(w, r.Recomputed)
325		if r.Consistent {
326			fmt.Fprintln(w, "consistent: yes")
327		} else {
328			fmt.Fprintln(w, "consistent: no (original and recomputed decisions differ)")
329		}
330	}
331	
332	func printDecision(w io.Writer, d darksafe.Decision) {
333		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  allowed: %v\n", d.Allowed)
334		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  reason: %q\n", d.Reason)
335		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  matched policies: %s\n", formatMatched(d.Matched))
336		fmt.Fprintf(w, "  policy version: %d\n", d.Version)
337	}

339	// formatMatched quotes each matched policy identifier byte-for-byte. A nil
340	// and an empty list mean the same set of hits but keep distinguishable
341	// spellings, mirroring the library's own nil-versus-empty preservation.
342	func formatMatched(matched []string) string {
343		if matched == nil {
344			return "[]"
345		}
346		out := "["
347		for i, id := range matched {
348			if i > 0 {
349				out += ", "
350			}
351			out += strconv.Quote(id)
352		}
353		return out + "]"
354	}

1	// This file implements lossless archiving of one organization's audit
2	// export. AuditExport hands back detached in-memory records and the caller
3	// separately retains the checkpoint pinning them; an archive serializes the
4	// export so it can be saved to a file when the service instance ends and
5	// read back later, still paired with the caller's own checkpoint and still
6	// usable as the material for RecheckDecisionOffline.
7	//
8	// The format is a length-delimited binary encoding built by hand rather
9	// than encoding/json: JSON text cannot carry bytes that are not valid
10	// UTF-8 without silently replacing them with U+FFFD, which would collapse
11	// genuinely different content (a lone 0xFF, a lone 0xFE and a real U+FFFD)
12	// onto identical records and change their fingerprints. Every string is
13	// written from its exact bytes with a length prefix, and nil slices,
14	// non-nil empty slices and absent payloads are each marked explicitly.
15	//
16	// Integrity never comes from trust in the file. A decode reconstructs the
17	// records and then runs the same whole-material VerifyAudit chain check
18	// against the checkpoint the caller supplies independently; the checkpoint
19	// embedded in the archive is informational only and never authoritative.
20	package darksafe
21	
22	import (
23		"bytes"
24		"crypto/sha256"
25		"encoding/binary"
26		"errors"
27		"fmt"
28	)
29	
30	// ErrInvalidArchive means archive bytes are not a recognizable, complete,
31	// untampered audit archive: a foreign/truncated/trailing-byte framing, a
32	// failed checksum, or content that does not decode. Content-level failures
33	// (missing or mismatched organization, missing, out-of-order or modified
34	// records, a mismatched checkpoint) keep using ErrMissingOrganization and
35	// ErrInvalidRange exactly as the other audit entry points do.
36	var ErrInvalidArchive = errors.New("darksafe: invalid audit archive")
37	
38	// Archive framing:
39	//
40	//	magic   = archiveMagic
41	//	u32 BE  = byte length of the payload that follows
42	//	payload = archivePayloadLen bytes
43	//	32 bytes = SHA-256 checksum of payload
44	//
45	// A second archive concatenated to a first is trailing material, not a
46	// second frame: a read consumes exactly one frame and rejects any byte
47	// beyond it.
48	const archiveMagic = "darksafe-audit-archive-v1\n"
49	
50	const (
51		archiveTagBoolFalse byte = 0
52		archiveTagBoolTrue  byte = 1
53		archiveTagNil       byte = 0
54		archiveTagPresent   byte = 1
55	)

57	// archiveWriter appends length-delimited fields to a byte buffer.
58	type archiveWriter struct {
59		buf []byte
60		err error
61	}

65	}

102	// validated, replaced or normalized: a lone 0xFF reaches the output as
103	// itself and stays distinguishable from 0xFE and a genuine U+FFFD.
104	func (w *archiveWriter) stringField(s string) {

113	// archive's field order is the fingerprint's order by construction. Even the

116	// table and therefore cannot move a fingerprint boundary.

132	// decode never has to reconstruct a shape. A present payload walks the

134	// fingerprint's order by construction and every change field round trips.

152	}

155	// VerifyAudit only ever accepts a decision payload on a decision record and
156	// its absence otherwise, but the distinction is encoded explicitly so decode
157	// never has to reconstruct a shape. A present payload walks the single
158	// decision field table, so the archive's field order is the fingerprint's
159	// order by construction and every request and decision field round trips.
160	func (w *archiveWriter) decisionRecord(d *DecisionRecord) {
161		if d == nil {
162			w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagNil)
163			return
164		}
165		w.buf = append(w.buf, archiveTagPresent)
166		for i := range decisionFields {
167			f := &decisionFields[i]

169			case decisionFieldString:

171			case decisionFieldStringList:
172				writeListShape(w, f.getList(d), w.stringField)

174				w.boolean(f.getBool(d))
175			case decisionFieldInt:

177			}
178		}
179	}

181	// EncodeAuditArchive serializes one complete audit export into savable
182	// bytes. org is the organization name, records is its complete chain from
183	// sequence 1 (a valid prefix ending at some historical sequence is enough,
184	// provided cp pins exactly that sequence), and cp is the checkpoint the
185	// caller separately retains. An organization with no records archives too:
186	// records is empty and cp is its sequence-0 genesis checkpoint.
187	//
188	// The whole material is validated exactly as VerifyAudit would before any
189	// bytes are returned: a missing organization is ErrMissingOrganization, and
190	// a missing, out-of-order or foreign record, modified content or checkpoint

192	// The checkpoint is carried in the archive for reference, but never stands
193	// in for the separately retained evidence: DecodeAuditArchive always
194	// validates against the checkpoint handed to it. The call is read-only:

197	func EncodeAuditArchive(org string, records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint) ([]byte, error) {
198		if org == "" {
199			return nil, ErrMissingOrganization
200		}
201		if err := VerifyAudit(org, records, cp); err != nil {

203		}

213			// the archive's record layout is the fingerprint envelope's layout
214			// — plus the record's own fingerprint, which the envelope excludes
215			// — by construction, and no outer field can be skipped or
216			// reordered here alone.
217			for j := range recordFields {

247	// archiveReader walks one payload without copying string contents: string
248	// fields are backed by the payload slice itself, which is owned by the
249	// decoder and never returned, so callers cannot mutate the input through

252		data []byte
253		pos  int
254		err  error
255	}
256	
257	func (r *archiveReader) need(n int) bool {
258		if r.err != nil {
259			return false
260		}

266	}

268	func (r *archiveReader) marker() byte {
269		if !r.need(1) {
270			return 0
271		}
272		b := r.data[r.pos]
273		r.pos++
274		return b
275	}
276	
277	func (r *archiveReader) u32() int {
278		if !r.need(4) {
279			return 0
280		}
281		v := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(r.data[r.pos : r.pos+4]))

287	// remain per item, so a hostile payload cannot drive a huge allocation
288	// with a count its body could never satisfy.
289	func (r *archiveReader) boundedCount(minBytesPerItem int) int {
290		n := r.u32()
291		if r.err != nil {
292			return 0
293		}
294		if n < 0 || uint64(n)*uint64(minBytesPerItem) > uint64(len(r.data)-r.pos) {

297		}
298		return n
299	}

301	func (r *archiveReader) boolean() bool {
302		switch r.marker() {
303		case archiveTagBoolTrue:
304			return true
305		case archiveTagBoolFalse:
306			return false
307		default:
308			if r.err == nil {
309				r.err = fmt.Errorf("%w: invalid boolean marker", ErrInvalidArchive)
310			}
311			return false
312		}
313	}
314	
315	func (r *archiveReader) stringField() string {
316		n := r.u32()
317		if r.err != nil {
318			return ""
319		}
320		if !r.need(n) {
321			return ""
322		}
323		// Conversion copies the bytes, so the result never aliases the input.
324		s := string(r.data[r.pos : r.pos+n])
325		r.pos += n
326		return s
327	}

329	// readList reads one length-counted list framed by writeListShape on the
330	// archive sink, whatever its item type: both string lists and the policy
331	// list decode here. Every list

333	// per-item byte floor before any allocation, and each item's own
334	// truncation/structure errors — so a hostile count can neither drive a
335	// disproportionate allocation nor deliver a partial list: once an item
336	// fails, the reader's sticky error fails the whole read.
337	// minBytesPerItem is the minimum an item could occupy (each string item
338	// carries one length word; a policy item carries six length words and a
339	// bool), and is used only to reject counts the remaining bytes could never
340	// satisfy.
341	func readList[T any](r *archiveReader, minBytesPerItem int, readItem func() T) []T {
342		switch r.marker() {
343		case archiveTagNil:
344			return nil
345		case archiveTagPresent:

361	}

363	func (r *archiveReader) policy() Policy {
364		// Read fields in the single table's (write and fingerprint) order. The
365		// fingerprint-optional ResourceID is still a mandatory, fixed field on

406		}
407		return c
408	}

411		switch r.marker() {
412		case archiveTagNil:
413			return nil
414		case archiveTagPresent:

425			f := &decisionFields[i]

427			case decisionFieldString:
428				f.setString(d, r.stringField())
429			case decisionFieldStringList:
430				// Each string item carries at least one length word.
431				f.setList(d, readList(r, 4, r.stringField))
432			case decisionFieldBool:
433				f.setBool(d, r.boolean())
434			case decisionFieldInt:
435				f.setInt(d, r.u32())
436			}
437		}
438		return d
439	}

441	// DecodeAuditArchive reads one archive produced by EncodeAuditArchive and
442	// returns records that can be handed directly to RecheckDecisionOffline.
443	// org is the organization the caller expects, and cp is the checkpoint the
444	// caller independently retained; the checkpoint embedded in the file is
445	// never treated as evidence, so even an archive carrying a plausible
446	// checkpoint only validates against the one supplied here.
447	//
448	// A missing organization is ErrMissingOrganization. Unrecognized framing,
449	// truncation, a trailing second archive or any other extra byte, a bad
450	// checksum, and undecodable content are ErrInvalidArchive. Records that
451	// decode but are missing, out of order, foreign to the organization,
452	// modified (including a record after the one the caller intends to review)
453	// or mismatched with the supplied checkpoint fail the whole read with
454	// ErrInvalidRange. Failure returns no records. A successful read only
455	// proves the material matches the checkpoint: an original decision that
456	// disagrees with a recomputed one is reported later by offline review, not
457	// treated as archive damage. The result is detached from archive (mutating
458	// one never reaches the other), and the call is read-only.
459	func DecodeAuditArchive(archive []byte, org string, cp Checkpoint) ([]AuditRecord, error) {
460		if org == "" {
461			return nil, ErrMissingOrganization
462		}
463		magicLen := len(archiveMagic)
464		if len(archive) < magicLen+4+sha256.Size || string(archive[:magicLen]) != archiveMagic {
465			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unrecognized audit archive", ErrInvalidArchive)
466		}
467		pos := magicLen
468		payloadLen := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(archive[pos : pos+4]))
469		pos += 4
470		checksumEnd := pos + payloadLen
471		if payloadLen < 0 || checksumEnd+sha256.Size != len(archive) {
472			// A short frame is truncation; bytes beyond the one frame (a
473			// concatenated second archive, junk appended to a good file) are a
474			// framing failure too.
475			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: truncated or trailing audit archive bytes", ErrInvalidArchive)
476		}
477		payload := archive[pos:checksumEnd]
478		sum := sha256.Sum256(payload)
479		if !bytes.Equal(sum[:], archive[checksumEnd:checksumEnd+sha256.Size]) {
480			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: checksum mismatch", ErrInvalidArchive)
481		}
482	
483		r := &archiveReader{data: payload}
484		embeddedOrg := r.stringField()
485		embeddedEndSeq := r.u32()
486		embeddedFingerprint := r.stringField()
487		// Every record writes two payload markers, a sequence word, two
488		// fingerprint length words and org/kind length words: 22 bytes even
489		// when every string is empty.
490		n := r.boundedCount(22)
491		if r.err != nil {
492			return nil, r.err
493		}
494		records := make([]AuditRecord, 0, n)
495		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
496			// Read the outer fields in the single record field table's (write
497			// and fingerprint) order, so a field can never be restored into
498			// the wrong member or skipped.
499			var rec AuditRecord
500			for j := range recordFields {
501				f := &recordFields[j]
502				switch f.kind {
503				case recordFieldString:
504					f.setString(&rec, r.stringField())
505				case recordFieldInt:
506					f.setInt(&rec, r.u32())
507				case recordFieldChange:
508					f.setChange(&rec, r.change())
509				case recordFieldDecision:
510					f.setDecision(&rec, r.decisionRecord())
511				}
512			}
513			records = append(records, rec)
514		}
515		if r.err != nil {
516			return nil, r.err
517		}
518		if r.pos != len(payload) {
519			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %d unconsumed archive bytes", ErrInvalidArchive, len(payload)-r.pos)
520		}
521	
522		// Content checks reuse the exact audit-range validation the live export
523		// and offline review paths use, so an archive can never smuggle in a
524		// shape those entry points would reject.
525		if embeddedOrg != org {

529		// header means the payload was altered, and the authoritative check
530		// below always uses the caller's independently retained checkpoint.

536		}

1	// Command scope_deny_override is the cross-scope worked example for the
2	// organization-level deny-overrides rule. It uses only the public Store API
3	// and the Go standard library, creates its own in-memory store, publishes
4	// real policy versions, and prints the full policy set and request next to
5	// every decision so the configuration can be compared directly with the
6	// result.
7	//
8	// Run with:
9	//
10	//	go run ./examples/scope_deny_override
11	//
12	// The program takes no arguments, writes no files, and works fully offline.
13	// One organization (acme), one enabled subject (u1), one resource (doc-1),
14	// one action (read). Three full-set publishes drive three cases:
15	//
16	//  1. A recursive deny on org/a and an exact allow on org/a/b are published
17	//     together as version 1. The read of doc-1 in org/a/b matches BOTH: the
18	//     parent deny reaches the child scope, and the verdict is a denial whose
19	//     hit list keeps both identifiers (sorted ascending) at version 1.
20	//  2. The same set is republished with the parent deny made non-recursive
21	//     (version 2). The deny then covers org/a alone; the child read matches
22	//     only the child allow and is allowed.
23	//  3. Version 3 keeps the recursive deny on org/a and instead adds an exact
24	//     allow on org/ab. org/ab is a slash-segment sibling, not a descendant
25	//     of org/a, so the deny cannot match and the org/ab read is allowed by
26	//     its own exact allow alone.
27	package main
28	
29	import (
30		"fmt"
31		"os"
32	
33		"github.com/asdhoaiqqq/darksafe-access/darksafe"
34	)
35	
36	func main() {
37		if err := run(); err != nil {
38			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "scope deny override example: failed:", err)
39			os.Exit(1)
40		}
41	}
42	
43	func run() error {
44		// One organization, one subject, one resource id, one action. The subject
45		// carries no roles at all: roles belong to the demo Access entry point and
46		// are never consulted by Store.Decide.
47		const (
48			org        = "acme"
49			subjectID  = "u1"
50			resourceID = "doc-1"
51			actionRead = "read"
52	
53			parentScope  = "org/a"
54			childScope   = "org/a/b"
55			siblingScope = "org/ab"
56	
57			childAllowID   = "a-child-allow"
58			parentDenyID   = "z-parent-deny"
59			siblingAllowID = "ab-exact-allow"
60		)
61	
62		store := darksafe.NewStore()
63	
64		// Case 1: one publish carries both policies. The child allow is exact on
65		// org/a/b; the parent deny is recursive on org/a, so it covers the whole
66		// slash-separated subtree, including org/a/b.
67		fmt.Println("case 1: recursive parent deny vs more specific child allow")
68		policiesV1 := []darksafe.Policy{
69			{ID: childAllowID, Subject: subjectID, Action: actionRead, Scope: childScope, Effect: darksafe.EffectAllow},
70			{ID: parentDenyID, Subject: subjectID, Action: actionRead, Scope: parentScope, Effect: darksafe.EffectDeny, Recursive: true},
71		}
72		v1, err := store.Publish(org, 0, policiesV1) // 0: the org has never published
73		if err != nil {
74			return fmt.Errorf("publish version 1: %w", err)
75		}
76		printPolicySet(v1, policiesV1)
77		childReq := readRequest(org, subjectID, resourceID, childScope, actionRead)
78		printRequest(org, childReq)
79		printDecision(store.Decide(org, childReq))
80		fmt.Println()
81	
82		// Case 2: republish the COMPLETE set with the parent deny made
83		// non-recursive. expectedVersion is the current version (1); the new set
84		// becomes version 2. A non-recursive policy covers its exact scope only.
85		fmt.Println("case 2: parent deny made non-recursive, same child read")
86		policiesV2 := []darksafe.Policy{
87			{ID: childAllowID, Subject: subjectID, Action: actionRead, Scope: childScope, Effect: darksafe.EffectAllow},
88			{ID: parentDenyID, Subject: subjectID, Action: actionRead, Scope: parentScope, Effect: darksafe.EffectDeny, Recursive: false},
89		}
90		v2, err := store.Publish(org, v1, policiesV2)
91		if err != nil {
92			return fmt.Errorf("publish version 2: %w", err)
93		}
94		printPolicySet(v2, policiesV2)
95		printRequest(org, childReq) // identical request: only the policy set changed
96		printDecision(store.Decide(org, childReq))
97		fmt.Println()
98	
99		// Case 3: recursive deny back in force, plus an exact allow for org/ab.
100		// Matching is by slash-separated segments: org/ab is not below org/a.
101		fmt.Println("case 3: recursive deny on org/a cannot reach the sibling scope org/ab")
102		policiesV3 := []darksafe.Policy{
103			{ID: parentDenyID, Subject: subjectID, Action: actionRead, Scope: parentScope, Effect: darksafe.EffectDeny, Recursive: true},
104			{ID: siblingAllowID, Subject: subjectID, Action: actionRead, Scope: siblingScope, Effect: darksafe.EffectAllow},
105		}
106		v3, err := store.Publish(org, v2, policiesV3)
107		if err != nil {
108			return fmt.Errorf("publish version 3: %w", err)
109		}
110		printPolicySet(v3, policiesV3)
111		siblingReq := readRequest(org, subjectID, resourceID, siblingScope, actionRead)
112		printRequest(org, siblingReq)
113		printDecision(store.Decide(org, siblingReq))
114		return nil
115	}
116	
117	// readRequest builds an envelope-valid request: subject org and resource org
118	// both equal the decision organization, and the subject is enabled.
119	func readRequest(org, subjectID, resourceID, scope, action string) darksafe.OrgRequest {
120		return darksafe.OrgRequest{
121			SubjectOrg:  org,
122			ResourceOrg: org,
123			Subject:     darksafe.Subject{ID: subjectID, Kind: "user"}, // Disabled defaults to false
124			Resource:    darksafe.Resource{ID: resourceID, Scope: scope},
125			Action:      action,
126		}
127	}
128	
129	// printPolicySet prints every field that participates in matching, including
130	// the empty resource-id, so "no resource restriction" is visible instead of
131	// assumed.
132	func printPolicySet(version int, policies []darksafe.Policy) {
133		fmt.Printf("  published as version %d (%d policies):\n", version, len(policies))
134		for _, p := range policies {
135			fmt.Printf("    policy id=%q subject=%q action=%q scope=%q effect=%q recursive=%v resource-id=%q\n",
136				p.ID, p.Subject, p.Action, p.Scope, p.Effect, p.Recursive, p.ResourceID)
137		}
138	}
139	
140	// printRequest prints the complete request envelope next to the policies, so
141	// nothing has to be reconstructed by the reader.
142	func printRequest(org string, req darksafe.OrgRequest) {
143		fmt.Printf("  request: decision-org=%q subject-org=%q resource-org=%q subject=%q disabled=%v resource=%q scope=%q action=%q\n",
144			org, req.SubjectOrg, req.ResourceOrg, req.Subject.ID, req.Subject.Disabled,
145			req.Resource.ID, req.Resource.Scope, req.Action)
146	}
147	
148	// printDecision prints the four decision fields: allowed or not, the reason,
149	// every matched policy identifier, and the published version actually used.
150	func printDecision(d darksafe.Decision) {
151		fmt.Printf("  decide : allowed=%v reason=%q matched=%q version=%d\n",
152			d.Allowed, d.Reason, d.Matched, d.Version)
153	}
